newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finland sees FIM 100-130 mln savings on upgrade.
newsitem.headline: Finland sees FIM 100-130 mln savings on upgrade.

text.p: Finland on Tuesday welcomed Standard&Poor's upgrade of its foreign currency debt, saying it would lower debt servicing costs by 100 million to 130 million markka over the next few years.
Kari Nars, the ministry's finance director, described the S&P move as a "nice Christmas gift."
"It is a tribute to the economic policy conducted," he told Reuters.
The ministry said in a statement that the upgrading meant "approximately 100 to 130 million markka in savings for the government."

Next year, Finland's gross foreign currency borrowing will be equivalent to 20-30 billion markka and Finland will repay the equivalent of some 30 billion markka of old foreign currency debt taken earlier, it said.

S&P upped Finland's rating to AA from AA-minus, citing the government's progress in reducing fiscal deficits, slowing growth in the state debt and the government's commitment to further fiscal consolidation.
Nars said it was important that S&P said Finland appeared to be "one of the few countries that will easily meet the Maastricht deficit criteria".
"That was an important international recognition. It gives Finland a better seat to seek membership in EMU," he said.
He declined to comment on whether he expected Moody's Aa2 rating to be changed but noted that both institutes now have Finland at the third grade from the top.
Moody's issued its Aa2 rating for Finland in January 1992.
